title: Define multi-shipment lifecycle and billing cardinality; stop silent conflict-drop underbilling

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every distinct active outbound shipment is independently billable, while voided labels, return labels, and provider duplicates are excluded by the canonical shipment aggregate.
Two active shipments persist two frozen billing rows totaling $32, preserve $25 of shipment cost and $7 of margin, and remain distinct in HTML, XLSX, and CSV exports.

Generated counts and totals come from inserted PostgreSQL rows; a duplicate candidate fails loudly and a repeat attempt leaves two rows and $32 unchanged instead of silently conflict-dropping underbilling.
Voiding the first active outbound shipment keeps the order shipped; only the final void may reopen it, and canonical or external terminal evidence prevents reopening.
Migration 0068 changes uniqueness without rewriting billing rows, and its executable rollback preserves the two current shipment rows while restoring the previous application duplicate constraint.
The focused PS-425 suite, all 45 mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and the production frontend build pass at the exact reviewed SHA.

The shipped-data override is narrowly documented, protections remain enforced, and verification performs no production billing regeneration, label purchase, postage charge, provider call, marketplace notification, or production shipped/cancelled mutation.

sotBypass.details: Billing generation and label void call the canonical backend shipment aggregate. Routes and exports only consume frozen rows; no frontend or route wrapper owns cardinality, lifecycle, cost, margin, or terminal-state truth.

evidence.proves: A PostgreSQL-compatible migrated fixture persists exactly two shipment-scoped billing rows totaling $32, reconciles $25 cost and $7 margin, and renders the same two shipment identities and charges in HTML, XLSX, and CSV.

Returns, voided replacements, and duplicate provider shipment identities cannot enter the active outbound set; a duplicate billing candidate fails loudly, a repeat leaves count and total unchanged, first-void remains shipped, and terminal evidence prevents an unsafe reopen.
Migration 0068 applies to a legacy-shaped billing table and replaces order-level uniqueness with shipment-aware and shipment-less partial unique indexes without rewriting fixture billing data.
The controlled rollback SQL drops both new indexes, restores billing_li_unique, preserves the two existing shipment rows and $32 total, accepts a legacy-shaped row, and rejects its duplicate.
The source-of-truth placement guard and executable migrated-database cardinality, lifecycle, export, repeat-run, and rollback proof execute together at the reviewed SHA.
All 45 mandatory source-of-truth, finalized-billing, lifecycle, runtime-schema, worker, and safety guards pass at the exact reviewed SHA.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully with 2,977 modules transformed.

The implementation is scoped to shipment aggregation, billing cardinality/read models/exports, aggregate-aware void lifecycle, migration, and offline tests. Locked labels logic carries the required user-override comment; no destructive shipped/cancelled guard, history, or schema protection was removed.

migrations.rollbackPlan: Stop Billing generation, run docs/final-review/evidence/PS-425-migration-rollback.sql transactionally, then deploy the previous application. The rollback removes the two PS-425 partial indexes, restores billing_li_unique (order_id, line_type, description), and preserves existing billing rows; the offline fixture proves both row preservation and legacy duplicate enforcement.

rollback.strategy: Stop Billing generation, apply the tested PS-425 rollback SQL, verify billing row count and total, then revert the packet, rollback-evidence, and implementation commits before redeploying. Do not regenerate finalized billing rows or rewrite shipment history.

liveVerification.reason: Cardinality, lifecycle, exports, repeat behavior, and migration rollback are executable against an in-memory PostgreSQL-compatible migrated fixture. No live provider, label purchase, postage, marketplace notification, production billing regeneration, or production shipped/cancelled mutation is needed for closure; deployment health is checked separately after push.
